stem: Two straight paths, \(AD\) and \(BE\), cross at point \(C\) in a park. Fences \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{DE}\) complete two triangular lawns, as shown. Angle \(CAB\) measures \(42^{\circ}\), angle \(ABC\) measures \(57^{\circ}\), and angle \(CDE\) measures \(35^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(CED\)?
solution: Angles \(ACB\) and \(DCE\) are vertical angles, so angle \(DCE = 81^{\circ}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 81 is the measure of angle \(DCE\); the question asks for angle \(CED\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This uses \(180 - 81 = 99\) for angle \(DCE\); vertical angles are equal, not supplementary.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(81 - 35\); the third angle of triangle \(CDE\) is \(180 - 81 - 35\).

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(P['A'][0]*P['D'][1]-P['A'][1]*P['D'][0])<0.01 and abs(P['B'][0]*P['E'][1]-P['B'][1]*P['E'][0])<0.01
assert abs(ang('C','A','B')-42)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','B','C')-57)<0.1 and abs(ang('C','D','E')-35)<0.1
ans=180-(180-42-57)-35
assert abs(ang('C','E','D')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==64
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
